text:
alex: Heads-up — eu-central1-b is showing a spike in GPU attach failures (~30%) over the last 20m. Lots of nodes reporting long NVMe background GC pauses and occasional firmware reset messages in dmesg.

taylor: saw this too on the dashboard. p95 write latency shot up around 00:42 UTC. Any isolated error logs?

alex: example dmesg: `nvme0: completing async command due to controller reset` and `nvme0n1: background_gc: start gc run length=...` Also `nvme error_count` increments on several drives.

jamie: is this the nightly backup window + janitor scrub overlap again or something different?

alex: different flavor — vendor notes that certain firmware will kick aggressive internal GC when the device's free block pool dips below threshold. We probably pushed a lot of short-lived checkpoints + backup snapshot writes.

priya: ops timeline: backups kicked at 00:40, qc-scrub at 00:45, and a large model training allocation began checkpointing at 00:46. Bad overlap.

infra-bot: alert: region eu-central1-b attach_failure_rate=29% at 1767088895 :rotating_light:

alex: immediate mitigation suggestions: (1) pause backup snapshot job in eu-central1-b for 2 hours; (2) throttle scrub runner to concurrency=2 in that AZ; (3) set scheduler to hold new GPU attaches in eu-central1-b for 15 minutes and route to eu-west1 where capacity exists.

taylor: pause backups now? that'll delay customer backups but avoid failed attaches. We'll notify CS.

jamie: we should also mark drives with error_count delta > 20 as replacement candidates and get vendor ticket open. We'll collect `nvme smart-log` for the set.

priya: applying backup pause: `POST /ops/policies/pause` payload sent for eu-central1-b backups by priya at 1767088905.

storage-bot: scrub concurrency updated for eu-central1-b: concurrency=2 by priya at 1767088910 :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: scheduler hold: new GPU attaches in eu-central1-b will be routed to fallback zones for 15m at 1767088912 by taylor

alex: quick canary of 10 attaches rerouted — 9/10 success. p95 write latency trending down. Good early sign.

taylor: estimate cost for 15m cross-region: ~+3% for these runs. finance, please note for reconciliation.

finance: acknowledged. will tag costs to incident-1767088888 and surface in bill-run.

jamie: collecting diagnostics: `for node in $(cat impacted.txt); do nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1 > /mnt/diag/$node-smart.log; dmesg | grep -i nvme > /mnt/diag/$node-dmesg.log; done` Uploading to /mnt/diag/1767088888/ at 1767088918.

alex: next steps: vendor escalation for drives with GC anomalies, schedule node replacements for any host with recurring readonly remounts, add a scheduler heuristic to avoid heavy background IO during known checkpoint windows (per-customer), and add alert for `nvme error_count delta > 10 in 1h` as an early-warning.

priya: noted. I'll create the vendor ticket and schedule replacements for the top 15 nodes.

storage-bot: vendor ticket created: VEND-8923. referencing logs at /mnt/diag/1767088888/.

alex: thanks. we'll keep the hold active until metrics stable for 30m. updating incident doc now.

infra-bot: hold extended until 1767089300 (manual) — will auto-resume if metrics OK earlier.

jamie: postmortem items: (a) avoid backup+scrub+checkpoint overlap via global orchestration; (b) soft-limit aggressive GC firmware cohorts with lower usable blocks; (c) improve attachment logic to prefer nodes with lower recent write dwell.

alex: good call. tagging CS to inform impacted customers and scheduling a follow-up meeting tomorrow. :thumbsup:
